label: ai logs for week 9 (cont.)
topic: Fixed HR account lockout, profile/announcement centralisation, employee invitation and bulk yearly entitlement in the Leave Management System; then made the password-reset and invitation links send as real SMTP email

content: Provided a handoff summary of the previous session (backend/ and frontend/ had been wholesale replaced with Member 1's file bundle, leaving the app non-runnable) and listed five issues to fix: "HR can get locked out of account and no one can unlock the HR's account. Each accounts' profile and the announcement banner needs to be improved. Employee invitation and bulk yearly entitlement not working." Requested changes: add a way for one of the managers to unlock the HR account; centralise each account's profile screen and announcement banner; make each profile display all current information and change correctly when prompted; make the employee invitation link work and create the send-link form; ensure the bulk yearly entitlement works.

Checked the repo first and confirmed nothing had changed since the previous session — still only Member 1's slice, with backend routes/{leaveRequest,publicHoliday,ai,notification,delegation,coverage,admin,report,swap}.js, models LeaveRequest/Notification/LeavePolicy/LeaveBalance/ConfigAuditLog, services mailer/notificationService/reportScheduleService, and frontend pages Employee.jsx/Approver.jsx/Admin.jsx all absent, so the backend could not boot and the frontend could not compile. Pointed out that two of the five issues (invitation form, bulk entitlement) live on the HR Admin page that exists only as a reference-only .txt snippet, and asked how to proceed; user chose to have minimal placeholder pages built now so the fixes would be testable. Root-caused issue 1 by reading middlewares/auth.js and routes/user.js: PUT /user/:id/unlock and /:id/force-logout were guarded by requireRole("HR_ADMIN") alone, so a locked-out HR account genuinely had no path back in — added MANAGER to both guards, added a new GET /user/locked endpoint (MANAGER + HR_ADMIN) listing currently-locked accounts, and added an "UNLOCKED" value to the SecurityEvent enum so the unlock is audited. For issues 2 and 3, found the profile and announcement banner were already centralised in App.jsx (one ProfilePanel and one AnnouncementBanner shared by every role), so the real defect was that PUT /user/profile never recomputed `initials` after a name change, leaving the header avatar stale — fixed it to recompute via initialsOf() and to return initials in the response. For issues 4 and 5, found the actual causes: routes/invitation.js was reusing sendResetEmail(), which builds a ?resetToken= link, while Login.jsx only opens the accept-invitation form on ?inviteToken= — so the invite link could never work; and the endpoint the bulk-entitlement button calls (/admin/entitlement/commit) did not exist at all. Wrote services/mailer.js with separate sendResetEmail/sendInviteEmail builders, created routes/admin.js (GET /admin/users, GET /admin/entitlement/preview, POST /admin/entitlement/commit), and built the missing send-link form into a new Admin.jsx. To make any of it runnable, also created minimal LeavePolicy, LeaveBalance and ConfigAuditLog models (referenced throughout Member 1's code but owned by other members' verticals), guarded User.associate against the still-missing LeaveRequest/Notification models, trimmed index.js to mount only routes that exist with a TODO marking where the rest go, commented out the two absent schedulers, removed a dead notificationService import, restored backend/.env and frontend/.env from the previous session's scratchpad backup, and wrote seed.js (10 country leave policies + the 9 demo accounts Login.jsx already advertises). Built placeholder Employee.jsx, Approver.jsx (including the manager-only locked-accounts panel) and Admin.jsx (accounts table with lockout badges and unlock/force-logout, invitation form, bulk-entitlement button, announcement composer). Since the sandbox had no database server, installed mysql-server, created the `leave` database using the credentials from the restored .env, and ran the seed. Then verified all five fixes end-to-end against the running API: locked the HR account out with three bad logins and confirmed even the correct password was refused, logged in as manager Diana, listed the locked account and unlocked it, and logged HR back in; sent an invitation and completed verify -> accept -> login as the new employee; ran the entitlement preview and commit and watched a pro-rated new joiner move from 3 to 7 days with ConfigAuditLog rows written; renamed HR from "Aisha" to "Aisha Rahman" and confirmed initials updated to "AR". Frontend build passed clean. Flagged that the app still needs the other members' files, and that installing MySQL was a system-level change contained to this dev environment.

content: "ensure that both the forget password link and employee link gets sent to an actual email"

Rewrote services/mailer.js for real delivery. Found a latent bug in the version written earlier in the session: it set neither `secure` nor `requireTLS`, so a port-465 provider would have hung — TLS is now derived from the port (465 implicit, 587/25 STARTTLS). Emails became proper multipart/alternative messages with an HTML template and a plaintext fallback, distinct copy per flow, HTML-escaped interpolation, and a verifyTransport() helper. Made the module never throw: every send returns { ok, demo, error, link }. That mattered because both callers write to the database before sending, so a bounced email previously 400-ed a request that had already mutated state — for invitations that left an orphaned INVITED account that could never be re-invited, because the email address was already taken. Updated POST /user/forgot-password to pass the user's name and to log a delivery failure server-side while keeping the response byte-identical whether or not the address exists, so the endpoint cannot be used as an account-enumeration oracle; also fixed its catch block, which returned { errors: undefined } for non-validation errors. Updated POST /invitation to report a delivery failure as an HTTP 207 partial success carrying the usable link, so HR is not stranded, and to record emailDelivered in the audit row. Fixed the blank-Start-date defect that had been deferred earlier, because it blocked this feature outright: yup's .matches() rejects an empty string by default, so the invite form 400-ed whenever HR left the optional date blank and no email could be sent at all — added excludeEmptyString and made a blank team fall back to the default instead of saving "". Added POST /invitation/:id/resend, which rotates the token and refreshes the 48-hour window, plus a per-row Resend button in Admin.jsx, since a failed first delivery was otherwise a dead end. Added scripts/mailtest.js with an npm run mail:test script that prints the configuration, authenticates, and optionally sends a live test, and made index.js announce at boot whether SMTP is live, because a silent demo-mode fallback is the usual reason emails 'never arrive'. Documented Gmail, Outlook, Brevo and Mailtrap setups in .env.example. Verified the delivery path without needing real credentials by writing a local SMTP server that speaks EHLO, STARTTLS, AUTH PLAIN and DATA with a self-signed certificate, then driving the real mailer through it: both messages transmitted over TLS with correct From/To/Subject and both MIME parts, the reset mail carried ?resetToken= and the invite ?inviteToken=. Then took the token out of the delivered reset email and actually used it — reset the password, logged in with the new one, and confirmed a replay is rejected as single-use — and confirmed resend rotates the token so the previous link is dead while the new one verifies. Also confirmed the offline demo-mode fallback still returns demoResetToken/demoInviteToken when SMTP is unset. Asked which provider to use; user chose Gmail with an App Password, so pre-filled backend/.env with smtp.gmail.com and step-by-step instructions while deliberately leaving SMTP_USER/SMTP_PASS blank, which keeps the app safely in demo mode until they are filled in, and confirmed .env is gitignored. Cleaned up the test accounts afterwards and restored the demo password that the reset test had changed.

content: "review again and check for any mistakes"

Reviewed the email work and found four real mistakes in code written this session, all in the assistant's own output. First and most serious: POST /invitation/:id/resend had no try/catch, and Express 4 does not catch rejections from async handlers, so a database error produced no response at all rather than a 500 — the request simply hung. Proved this two ways rather than asserting it: a minimal Express 4 reproduction where the unguarded route timed out with http_code 000 and logged an unhandledRejection while the guarded route returned a clean 500, and then against the real endpoint by stopping MySQL mid-request, which now correctly returns 500. Second: the same defect existed in three handlers written earlier in the session — GET /admin/users, GET /admin/entitlement/preview and GET /user/locked — meaning any database blip would hang the HR accounts table, the entitlement preview and the manager's locked-accounts panel; added try/catch to all three. Third: the first version of the resend fix echoed err.message straight to the client, which can expose internal detail, so it now logs server-side and returns a generic message. Fourth: smtpConfigured had been left imported in both route files after they switched to the mail.demo flag, so those imports were dead and were removed. Also added a warning when CLIENT_URL is unset, since that silently produces relative, unclickable links in emails. Separately checked the exact command that had been documented for the user, npm run mail:test you@email.com without a -- separator, having only tested it with --; confirmed both forms work on npm 11, so the documentation was correct. Re-ran the full surface after the fixes: syntax checks on every changed file, RBAC checks (locked-accounts endpoint 403 for an employee and 401 unauthenticated, resend 401 without a token, 404 for an unknown id, 400 on an already-accepted invitation), the 207 mail-failure path with SMTP pointed at a closed port, and confirmed the fallback link from that 207 fully activates an account through verify, accept and login. Frontend build passed. Reported two deliberate judgment calls rather than silently keeping them: HTTP 207 is unconventional for this purpose since it is really a WebDAV status, and the 207 body shows HR the raw SMTP error and the invite token, which is intended because HR needs both to recover. Also flagged that the same missing-try/catch pattern remains in handlers from the original bundle that were not written this session, and recommended a shared async wrapper over copying try/catch into each one. Cleaned up all review test data and confirmed the nine demo accounts were intact.

content: Please write a handoff summary for this session. Include: what we were working on and the current state, key decisions made and the reasoning behind them, files created or modified, what still needs to be done, and any known issues or things to watch out for.

Wrote a structured handoff summary distinguishing the two pieces of work: the five original fixes, which the user committed mid-session as 5d46ff9, and the email delivery work, which is still uncommitted. Covered the key decisions and their reasoning — widening the unlock guard to MANAGER because a locked HR account otherwise had no recovery path, building placeholder pages so the fixes could be tested rather than waiting for teammates' files, stubbing the three cross-vertical models and installing MySQL locally so verification was possible at all, choosing Gmail with an App Password, making the mailer no-throw because both callers write to the database before sending, keeping forgot-password byte-identical on failure to avoid account enumeration, and returning 207 with the raw link so HR can still onboard someone after a delivery failure. Listed every file created and modified, split by whether it is committed. Set out the remaining work: add the Gmail credentials and verify with npm run mail:test, commit the email work, paste in the other members' routes/models/services and re-mount them, and replace the placeholder pages. Recorded the known issues, including the two bugs the user chose to defer — most importantly that GET /user/auth echoes the stale JWT payload instead of reading the database, so a profile rename reverts on refresh for up to the eight-hour token life, which is the same symptom as the original complaint — plus the MySQL root password sitting in plaintext in committed .claude/settings.json permission entries, bulk entitlement silently overwriting pro-rated entitlements, the pre-existing unguarded async handlers, this sandbox's MySQL stopping repeatedly and pkill collateral damage, emailed links depending on CLIENT_URL, and the bcrypt/mysql2 versus bcryptjs/sqlite3 dialect mismatch with models/index.js hardcoding the mysql dialect while .env still carries DB_DIALECT/DB_STORAGE.
